replies: After ninety days it is mine to sell.
I put it in the case. It stays in the case.

...Otis. Otis from the yard.
Then you go and tell him, because I am not walking up that street to say the sentence "I think I lent money against your ring" to a man I have said good morning to for fifty years.

topics.label: It is over.
replies: I heard it. Everybody on this street heard it.

Ryan owes one hundred thousand dollars to a filing cabinet.
Tell him. Do not tell him gently. He has spent nineteen years being told things gently.

topics.label: You are typing for her.
replies: I am typing for her, love. So are you now.

topics.label: I will let you get on.

npcs.bio: Works the loan window. Takes in a great many things, has never once had one collected, and answers a telephone in the back that does not ring for the shop.

npcs.name: Merle Tancredi

lines.text: Do you need a lift?
I am alright. It is not far.
Thank you though. People do stop. That is the thing about this road, people do stop.

replies: To the pumps? Twenty minutes. Twenty-five if I take it easy.
Twenty minutes.

topics.label: What happened to your car?
replies: Nothing happened to it. It is fine. It is back there.
...Because I got out.

That is the answer and it is not a good one and I have turned it over a great deal. I was driving, and then I was standing on the shoulder with the door open and the engine running, and there is nothing in between those two.
I did not go back for it. You will pass it. Do not go in it.

replies: Tankers. Going down. Never coming up, or never while I am looking, and I have been looking.
And a truck at about two, going the other way, doing about seventy, with nobody in it. I do not mean I could not see a driver. I mean I could see the seat.

topics.label: Mind how you go.
replies: You as well. And if you are going down that road — go down it. Do not stop on it. Stopping is what does it.

npcs.bio: Walking up to the pumps. Has been walking up to the pumps for a while now and is not troubled by it.

npcs.name: Dale Prewitt

lines.text: Long stretch.
Two coats. It wants two coats out here, the sun eats it.
You are the first vehicle I have had to wave past in eleven days, so take your time, I am in no rush and neither is the paint.

topics.label: How far do you take it?
replies: To the grid. Then I turn the truck round and I do the other side coming back.
Work order says to the grid.

Nineteen years of work orders and every one of them says to the grid. And here is the part I have never said to anybody: I have never once seen who signs them. They come through the office. Somebody puts them in the tray.
It is a good job. I am not complaining. I am answering the question you asked, which is a different thing, and I notice I have been waiting a while to be asked it.

topics.label: What is the road like past there?
replies: Painted. That is what gets me.
Somebody paints it. Not me and not the county, and it is a better line than mine — straighter than a man does it, and no joins in it anywhere. I have walked out and looked.
Everybody has to stop for joins. You have to lift the gun. There is a mark where you lift the gun and there is one every forty foot of every road in this state and there is not one out there.

topics.label: Who comes down here?
replies: Tankers. A grey bus with the windows done, twice a month, and it does not stop at the gate — the gate is open before it gets there.
And once a fella walking north who would not take a lift. Told him it was twelve miles. He said twenty minutes and thanked me very politely and kept going.

topics.label: I will let you paint.
replies: Mind the wet. — and if you are going along that wire, go along the wire and not over it. There is a difference and I would rather not know how I know that.

npcs.bio: Paints the centre line for the county. Paints it as far as the cattle grid and not one foot further.

npcs.name: Dr Winifred Alsop

lines.text: What is this?
Containment. You should not be in here and I am not going to be the one who stops you.
Look at it if you are going to look at it. Everybody does. It is why the room has a window.

topics.label: What have you learned in thirty-one years?
replies: That it does not age. That it does not need to eat and eats anyway, which I have four hundred pages on. That the tails are not prosthetic and are not vestigial and are not for balance.
I have run one thousand and forty structured interviews.
...No. I take your meaning and I do not accept it. A structured interview is asking.

topics.label: Why do you call her an alien?
replies: Because it came out of that ring, and the ring is not ours, and nothing that comes out of a thing that is not ours is ours.
Yes. I have noticed. I noticed in about nineteen sixty-one.

The file was already open by then. You cannot re-title a file. You can append to it, and I have appended eleven times, and the title is on the front and the appendices are at the back and nobody has ever read to the back.

topics.label: And the light in the other cage?
replies: That is the one I would like thirty-one years with.
It does nothing. It turns, it brightens, it goes quiet. And every so often it does the eight, and every time it does the eight the whole county goes dark and the power company files a fault.
I know. Reyes. I have read every one of her submissions and every one of them is correct and I have never replied to any of them, and I would like to tell you that was a decision.

topics.label: I have seen enough.
replies: So have I. That is not the same as being finished, which I have said out loud now and did not enjoy.

npcs.bio: Has kept the file since fifty-four. Three hundred pages, and the word "her" is not in any of them.

npcs.name: General Cordell Mabry

lines.text: General.
You are not on any list I have got.
Which is a problem for later. Ask me what you came down here to ask me, and then we will both have a difficult afternoon.

topics.label: Who authorised this?
replies: That is the question, is it not. I have been asking it for four years through a chain of command that goes up eleven links and then stops.
Stops at a signature block with no name in it and a routing code that no longer routes anywhere.
I sign the continuation order every October. I have signed four of them. I do not know who reads them and I have stopped putting that in writing.

topics.label: What are you afraid of?
replies: Not the specimen.
The specimen has been in that cage since before my father enlisted and has never once put a hand on the glass.

That it is patient. That is the whole of it. Everything in this building is on a clock — the fuel, the buses, the eight — and the only thing in here that is not in a hurry is the thing we are holding.

You do not wait thirty-one years for nothing. You wait for a date. And I sign the order in October, and the eight fires in October, and I have put those two facts on the same page exactly once and then I took the page home and burned it in a grill.

topics.label: Let her go.
replies: I have drafted that order.
It is in my desk. It has been in my desk for two years and it is signed and it is not dated, and every October I take it out and look at the empty box where the date goes.
Nothing stops me. That is what I would like you to understand. There is nobody above me on this and there has not been for years, and the reason that door is still locked is me.

topics.label: Good luck, General.
replies: I have not had any yet. I will let you know.

npcs.bio: Inherited the programme, the building and the file. Has not inherited anybody who can tell him how it started.

npcs.name: The Man in the Black Suit

lines.text: And you are?
Here.

topics.label: June says you never eat the breakfast.

Because a table of four men who order nothing is a table people remember, and a table of four men who order everything and eat nothing is a table people decide they did not look at properly.
That is not a trick. It is just true about people. We have found it works everywhere we have tried it, which is everywhere.

topics.label: Do you work for the General?
replies: No.
He suspects it, in the way a man suspects a draught. He has never gone looking for the window.
I would like to be clear that I have never lied to him. He has asked me eleven questions in four years and I have answered all eleven completely. He has not yet asked the twelfth.

topics.label: What is the fox to you?
replies: A guest.
Yes.
I notice you have not asked me what the ring is, and that is the better question, and I am going to answer the one you asked because that is the rule.

She is a guest. The cage is Doctor Alsop's. We supply the building and the power and the paperwork, and we have never once asked her to keep it locked, and it has been locked for thirty-one years, and that is a fact about your people and not about mine.

topics.label: Nothing further.
replies: There always is. Come back when you know which one it is.

npcs.bio: Does not give a name and is not being difficult about it. Eats breakfast at a diner ninety miles north every Thursday and does not eat it.

npcs.name: Ilsa

lines.text: You have the mark. On your chest. I can see it from here.
Sit down. Nobody in this room will stop us talking, and I have been saving quite a lot up.

topics.label: What is your name?

topics.label: They think you are an alien.

He wrote down that the specimen was displaying mimicry.
That is not stupidity. I want to be fair to them, which is a strange thing to be spending my time on. It is that they decided in the first fortnight, and everything since has had to fit.

topics.label: How did you get here?
replies: The same way you did, near enough. I came through the ring.

It was open for eight seconds. It is always open for eight seconds. I went through it on purpose because I was looking for somebody, and I came out in a room with a floor worn down by boots and four men already standing in it.
That is the one I am not going to answer yet. Not because I do not trust you. Because if I say it out loud in this room it goes in the file, and I have kept it out of the file for thirty-one years.

topics.label: And the light next door?
replies: She came through after me. About four years after, I think — they do not tell me the date and I stopped counting when I realised I was counting.

I do not know that. I say it because the alternative is "it", and I have had thirty-one years of being called "it" through a pane of glass and I am not going to be the second person in this building to do that to somebody.

She does eight. Every time. Eight, spaced out, and then she stops and she waits, and I have never once been able to answer her, and I think that is the cruellest thing in this building and nobody in it has noticed it is happening.

topics.label: I will come back.

Two years.

And I will say yes sir, because the alternative is saying it out loud to a review board, and I have watched what happens to the ones who do that.
You are not a review board. You are a hole in my fence.

npcs.role: Three hundred and eleven years old

Tell me the dream.
A fox. Too many tails to count, and then she is not a fox any more, she is a ball of light turning over and over. She is in a cage. She asks to be let out.

Which is how I found this town. Somebody in this desert is holding one of you. The dream comes from the north-west and it comes hardest in October, and there is exactly one thing north-west of here that is not on a map.

topics.label: Say the name, Hiro.
replies: You know the name. Everybody in the world knows the name — it is a joke on a bumper sticker.

It is forty miles that way behind a wire fence with a hole in it, and there is a woman on the road out there who has been counting lights coming out of the ground every October for eleven years, and her count and my dream are the same number.
Eight.

topics.label: Let me think about all this.
replies: Take your time, Godfather. I have had rather a lot of it.

replies: Eight of them. Cut in when they put the roof on, same crew, same week.

replies: The engineer. Never got a name off him, and I have been asking for nineteen years.

topics.label: Why out here?
replies: Because in there they turn you down when the tables get loud. Out here I am the loud thing.

topics.label: Nothing. Carry on.
replies: We will be here. We are always here.

replies: Nine years on this spot. Deke was here before me by ten.

replies: One. If you play sixty they stop hearing any of them.

replies: They stop for the floor. Every time. They come in off the Strip looking at their feet and the floor makes a noise and up comes the head.
Then they see us, and by then they have already stopped, so they stay.

lines.text: I got here first. I did say.
How?

topics.label: You said you were looking for somebody.
replies: I did. And I said I would not say it out loud in that room, and I am not in that room.
Three hundred years ago I gave something away in a city with a river through it. A small thing on a cord. It was mine and I did not need it and he did.
You know him.
Of course he has. He is wearing my name round his neck and he has never once wondered why the fox in the dream keeps looking at him.
I came through in fifty-four to find out where it had got to. I have been eleven hundred yards from it since about nineteen fifty-nine.

topics.label: And the light — is she all right?
replies: She is here. She is not going to be a shape you can talk to for a while and that is all right, we have got time now.
She did eight for thirty-one years into a room with nobody in it who could count.
Then he was listening, which is more than the building she was in ever managed, and I would like his name at some point.

topics.label: Come with me.
replies: No.
I have been through that ring once and it cost me seventy-one years, and the thing I went through it for is sitting in a boneyard four miles away with a tarp over the good stuff.
You go. I am going to go and stand in front of a very old man and let him find out he was right.
He will. He has been getting it in his sleep for thirty years and nobody has ever told him it was post.

topics.label: Open it.
replies: Stand back a little. It comes up hot and it does not care whose foot is where.

topics.label: Not yet.
replies: It has been down there seventy-one years. It will keep for another ten minutes.

npcs.name: Lena

lines.text: I heard you asking about Ryan. Who are you?
A fellow magician. I have to open for Ryan tonight, because he is missing.
He is more than missing. He is in trouble.
I saw four guys in black suits put him in the trunk of a black car and drive towards the desert.
I hope you can help him. I was never here. I said nothing.

topics.label: Four of them?
replies: Four. Black suits, and not the good kind — the kind that all came out of the same shop on the same afternoon.

topics.label: Why tell me?
replies: Because you asked. Nine years on that floor and you are the first person who came in and asked after somebody instead of after a table.
Two hundred and eleven names in my book, love. Nobody looked up. I looked up.

topics.label: You were never here.
replies: I was never here. I said nothing. Go on.

npcs.bio: Off the floor, out on the boulevard, and standing where the cameras are not.

npcs.name: CHOP

lines.text: That is far enough.
Wrong road, friend. There is nothing down here and there is nobody down here, and in about ten minutes there will be even less of both.

topics.label: Who are you?
replies: Nobody. That is the job. You do not get to be somebody and do this.
The house extends credit. Somebody has to go and collect it. Tonight that is four of us and a car.

topics.label: What is he to you?
replies: A number. He was a number when he sat down and he is a smaller one now.
Nineteen years that man has been sawing women in half and he still could not make eleven thousand dollars disappear.

topics.label: Nice suits.
replies: We get them done in town. All four at once, same afternoon.
You noticed that, did you. Everybody notices that.

npcs.bio: Front seat. Does the talking, which in this line of work is the senior job.

npcs.name: THE OTHER ONE
npcs.bio: Nobody has ever used his name in front of him and he has stopped expecting it.

npcs.name: MARTY
npcs.bio: Twenty-six. Has been told this is a driving job four separate times.

npcs.name: THE BIG ONE
npcs.bio: Carries the shovel. Has not been asked to use it yet tonight.

npcs.name: Ryan

lines.text: HEY! HEY — over here! Do not just STAND there, they have got a SHOVEL —
I am the opening act! I am DUE ON! Tell them I am due on!

npcs.bio: RYAN THE MAGNIFICENT. Nineteen years the opening act at the Showroom, and the only man on this road wearing a colour.

npcs.name: Ryan

lines.text: You are the one Vito put on in my place.
Somebody had to.
Nineteen years I have opened that room and the one night I miss, somebody walks on and does REAL magic. That is the business, kid. That is the whole business.
Right. I am walking back. Do not tell me how far it is.

topics.label: Eleven thousand dollars?
replies: Eleven thousand two hundred. The two hundred is the part that keeps me awake.
I will pay it. I have always paid it. That is why they keep extending it, and if you can see the shape of that you are already ahead of me.

topics.label: Can you still go on?
replies: Son, I have gone on with a broken wrist, a dead dove and a wife in the fourth row.
Get back to town. I will be along. Tell Vito to hold the doves — they know me and they do not know you.

topics.label: Go carefully.
replies: I will go quickly, which out here is the same thing.

npcs.bio: RYAN THE MAGNIFICENT, upright, filthy, and eleven thousand dollars lighter than he would like to be.

replies: He asked whether he might finish the hand. I said that he might.
He finished it, he tipped the dealer, and he thanked me by name at the door.
Across the boulevard, I imagine. They will not have him either, and he knew that, and he went anyway.
The politest ninety seconds of my working life, and I would not do it again for anything.

topics.label: The first floor is done.
replies: She goes up and looks. She does not say she is going to and she does not pretend she has not when she comes back.
"Every bed. Including the one in 104, which nobody does, because you cannot see it from the door."
"Everything is on the list. That is not the same as being done."

topics.label: Good evening.
replies: Good evening. Do come back through the front; the side door is for deliveries and I will know.

npcs.bio: Duty manager. Has asked four hundred people to leave this building and has never once done it without being able to show them why.

npcs.name: Sergeant Pell

lines.text: Evening.
Evening. Lost, robbed, or looking for work? It is one of the three at this hour.
Sit if you like. Nobody ever does. There are two chairs and I have watched a man stand for an hour beside both of them.

topics.label: Is there work?
replies: She turns the board round without getting up. Four lines on it and two of them have been crossed through and written again.

"A WALLET. Somebody handed in an empty one on Tuesday and the man it belongs to has been in twice since. It is out there on this street somewhere and I have four officers and none of them are looking."
"THREE EARS. The Captain wants three conversations listened to. He has not signed it yet, so it is not work, it is a note."
"THE LOAN WINDOW. Somebody inside it, which is a thing you do not volunteer for and a thing he has not signed either."
"FIND RYAN. Ryan the Magnificent, off the boulevard, and everybody on this street has an opinion about where and not one of them has a road."
"Do the ones that are signed and come back. Nobody has ever done all four."

topics.label: I have the wallet.
replies: She opens it, reads the card in it, and writes something in a book that already has nine thousand things in it.
"Vic Pesaro. Nineteen fifty-eight address, which means he has not moved, which means he is one of about four people in this town who has not."
"It was empty on Tuesday as well. He does not want the money, love, he wants the card."
"There is a finder’s sum. It is sixty dollars and it comes out of a line in the budget that has not been touched since before I got here."
"One down. Do not look so pleased."

topics.label: I found Ryan.
replies: She stops writing.
"...Walking."
"I have had that man’s name on this board since Thursday and four grown officers telling me the desert is a big place."
She crosses it off. She does it slowly, and she does it in ink.
"Two down, and one of them was the one that mattered. The Detective will want to hear it from you and I would let him ask."

topics.label: What is left on the board?
replies: "The two the Captain has not signed. He signs a thing when he can stand behind it in a room with the Mayor in it, and he cannot stand behind either of those yet."
"He will. He is the most serious man I have ever worked for and I have worked for some very tired ones."

topics.label: Thirty years on this street.
replies: "Thirty-one in March. I have watched four casinos change their names and one of them change it back."
"Has moved twice, which is two more times than it has closed."
"I know her name. I know all their names. Knowing a name and being able to write it in this book are two different jobs and I have only ever been paid for the second one."

topics.label: Good night, Sergeant.
replies: "Mind the step on the way out. Everybody says they will."

npcs.bio: Thirty-one years behind this counter in March. Knows every name on Fremont Street and has only ever been paid to write down the ones she can prove.

npcs.name: Detective Dick

lines.text: Detective?
Dick. Do not make the joke, I have heard the joke, the joke is older than you are.
Sit down. Or stand. Everybody stands.

topics.label: You are looking for somebody.
replies: He does not put the folder down.
"Ryan the Magnificent. Headline act, showroom, forty years, and then nine hours at a table and a black car on the north side."
"A woman with a tray, who did not tell me, and who I am not going to name in a building with an open door in it."
"I am Detective Dick. I have been on this street eleven years and I have never once had a case where everybody was so willing to be helpful about nothing."

topics.label: He is out. He is walking the highway.
replies: The folder goes down.
"...And you."
He looks at you for a while, and then he writes one line, and then he closes the folder on it.

"I am going to say something and you are going to let me finish it. I think you are hiding something. I have thought so since I heard your name the first time and I have not once been able to say what."
"Tonight I do not care. Tonight a man who was in a trunk is walking, and I have been doing this long enough to know the difference between a thing I can prove and a thing I am glad about."
"Come and see me after your next show."

topics.label: What is in the folder?
replies: "Eleven years of this street, and I will tell you the shape of it because the shape is not a secret. Everything on Fremont goes through one window and the window is legal."
"And every so often somebody in this building knows something four hours before I do."
He says that to the folder rather than to you.

topics.label: Later, Detective.
replies: "They all say later."

npcs.bio: Eleven years on this street and has never had a case where everybody was so willing to be helpful about nothing.

npcs.name: Officer Teague

lines.text: Officer.
Evening. Keep to the lit side and we will both have an easy night.

topics.label: Busy night?
replies: "Quiet. Fremont is always quiet if you walk it right."
"You want to know the trick? You do the west side first, then the mall, then the yard. You never do the boulevard end twice."

topics.label: The loan window moved.
replies: "Top of the street. Straight up — it is the whole end of the road." He says it without thinking and then he hears himself say it.
"...I walk a beat."
"It is a legitimate business. It has a licence on the wall and I have read it, which is more than anybody in here has done."
He is wearing a watch that costs more than the coat over it, and he catches you not looking at it, which is worse than being caught looking.
"Anyway. Long night."

topics.label: Nothing, Officer.
replies: "Right you are."

npcs.bio: Walks the west side first, then the mall, then the yard, and has never once been asked to swap.

npcs.name: Officer Kasprzak

lines.text: Busy?
Paperwork. It is always paperwork. The street is the easy half.

topics.label: How long have you been in?
replies: "Nine years, and eight of them out there." He points at the door with his chin, the way people do when their hands are full of nothing.
"It is a good street. It gets a name it does not deserve because everything that happens on it happens under a light."

topics.label: Is everybody here straight?
replies: "...That is a question."
"The Captain is. The Sergeant is, and she has had thirty years of reasons not to be. The Detective is straight in a way that makes him hard to be in a car with."
"And I do the west side first, then the mall, then the yard, and I have never once been asked to swap."
He goes back to the form he is filling in, and he fills it in properly, which takes a while.

topics.label: Stay safe.
replies: "On Fremont? Always."

npcs.bio: Nine years in and eight of them out there. Fills the form in properly, which takes a while.

npcs.name: Captain Delrose

lines.text: Captain.
Sit. No — do not sit, you will be up again in a minute and it will be awkward for both of us.
You are the one off the boulevard. I have had four people describe you to me tonight and all four of them said fox and then apologised for it.

topics.label: You take crime seriously.
replies: "I take it personally, which is worse and gets more done."
"There are four men and one sergeant in this building and there are eleven thousand people on this boulevard after midnight. Anybody who tells you that is a police force is selling you something."
"So I sign what I can stand behind. Two things on that board are not signed and they are not signed because I will not send a civilian at a woman on Fremont Street on a Tuesday and a hunch."

topics.label: One of your officers is on the take.
replies: He does not move and he does not blink and it costs him something.
"Say a name."

"No. Quite right. Do not say a name in this room until you can put the thing beside it on this desk, because the moment you say it I have to act on it, and if you are wrong I have destroyed a man who has a daughter."
"Bring me the thing. Not the name. The thing."
It is the first time all night anybody in this building has looked tired.

topics.label: What would make me an officer here?
replies: "Four jobs off that board and I will pin something on you myself, and the Mayor will come, and there will be a photograph of it in a paper "nobody reads."
"It is honorary. It carries no powers whatsoever and everybody on this street will behave as though it carries all of them, which is exactly why it is worth having."

topics.label: Captain.
replies: "Shut the door on the way. It sticks."

npcs.bio: Takes crime personally, which is worse than seriously and gets more done. Signs a thing when he can stand behind it in a room with the Mayor in it.

npcs.name: Ruthie

lines.text: Checking in, or just looking at the lift?

topics.label: Yes.
replies: You would like a room.
Everybody who comes through that door at this hour would like a room. Most of them would like it at four in the morning and would like it to have been free.
Comped. Do not look at me like that — it is not a favour, it is arithmetic. You came in through the floor, and the house has already worked out what the floor is going to get back.
Lift is behind you, three floors, take any door that opens. They all open.

topics.label: Which floor should I take?
replies: They are the same floor three times. That is not me being unhelpful, that is the building.
Two is quieter. One hears the floor and three hears the plant, and two hears whichever of those is louder tonight, which is a thing you can decide about after you have had a drink and not before.

topics.label: Do people ever not come back down?
replies: Every night. Not in the way you mean.
They come down at eleven the next morning with their shoes in their hand and they are extremely surprised about the time. That is nine thousand people and it has never once been a different story.
The ones I remember are the ones who go up early. Nobody in this building goes up early.

npcs.bio: Front desk. Has put nine thousand people in rooms and can tell you which of them came back down for breakfast.

npcs.name: The Pharaoh

lines.text: You came up in my lift, you walked past four of my people, and not one of them stopped you.
That was not an oversight. I wanted to see how you walked.
And?
You walk like somebody who has never once been asked to leave a building.
Sit down. ...No. You cannot, can you. The chairs in here were made for men.
They call me the Pharaoh. My name is Farrow. Nobody now living remembers which of those came first and I have given up correcting either one.
Now. You have been seen in a certain back room behind a certain pawn shop.
I have.
Good. That is not a problem. That is a qualification.

topics.label: The first one.
replies: Tonya Soprani keeps a place out past the cattle grid and I have known that for two years. What I have never known is WHICH place, and I am not going to learn it by asking.
Thursdays, two of hers go out there on foot from the road. You are going to be on that road.
Walk behind them. That is the entire job.
You will not touch them, you will not speak to them, and you will not go in after them. The day I want somebody inside that building I will send eleven people and a van.
Then they never go back there, I wait another two years, and I am extremely polite to you about it. You will find that is worse.

topics.label: I know where the safehouse is.
replies: He puts both hands flat on the desk, which is the most he has moved since you met him.
"Say it."
"The BLOCK house."
"There is a trailer. Three separate people have told me about a trailer and I have paid two of them."
"...There is no trailer, is there."
Two years. He sits with it for a moment and then counts a hundred and fifty out of the drawer without looking down.
"The second one starts with a bag. Come back when you have slept — I want you awake for it."

topics.label: They saw me.
replies: "Then they saw you. It happens."
"They will be out there again. They are always out there again — that is what a safehouse IS, it is a place people keep going to."
"Go back to the road. Stay off their shoulder and do not let the dark have them either."

topics.label: They call you the Pharaoh.
replies: They do. I own the only building on this boulevard with a point on the top of it, my name is Farrow, and one of those two facts came first.
I have been asked which about four thousand times and I have given four thousand different answers, and every one of them was better than the truth.
That my mother chose the name and my accountant chose the building.

topics.label: Why is everybody in pink?
replies: Because I can see them.

Tonya Soprani dresses her people in seven different colours and she will tell you it is so she can tell them apart. It is not. It is so that when one of them is standing somewhere he should not be, he is only ever ONE colour of wrong.
Mine are all one colour. A room with four of my people in it looks like a room with four of my people in it from the far end of a street.
Then I send somebody who is not wearing pink. This is the part of the conversation where you have a think about what you are wearing.

topics.label: Tonya Soprani.
replies: Tonya. Yes.
We have worked together. Twice a year, maybe three times, when a thing is too big for one family and too good to leave. It goes well. It has always gone well.
But there is a day coming when one of us is going to be told about the other one first, and whoever is told first is the one who is still here on the day after that.
She knows it. I know it. We are very warm about it. It is the most honest relationship either of us has.

topics.label: Nice building.
replies: It is a hotel with a light on it. The light does nothing. It cost more than the hotel.
Fourth of July, nineteen years ago, it went out for eleven minutes and the switchboard took two hundred calls. Two hundred people, ringing a hotel, about a light.
That is when I understood what I had actually bought.

topics.label: Is there work?
replies: There is always work. There are three things I want done and I want them done in an order.
The first one is a walk. You will not touch anybody and nobody will touch you, and if you do it properly nobody will ever know you were there at all.
The second one is a drive, and a shovel.
The third is not a walk and it is not a drive.
Go downstairs. Have a drink on the house, look at the light, and come back up. I will have decided which of the three I trust you with first.

npcs.bio: Augustus Farrow. Owns the Pyramid, the light on top of it and a great deal of what goes on underneath it. Has not stood up for anybody in nineteen years and does not intend to start.

npcs.name: Mr Sable

lines.text: You are closer to him than most people get.
I would not make a thing of it. He is in a good mood and a good mood on that man is weather.

topics.label: Housekeeping is not your job.
replies: "It is tonight."
"Because a cleaner goes in every room on a floor and nobody in this building thinks twice about it. That is the most useful thing a person can be in a hotel and it costs a hundred dollars."
"I am not asking you to look at anything. I am asking you to clean. What you happen to see is your business until it is mine."

topics.label: What is he like to work for?
replies: "Fair. Slow to decide and impossible to move after."
"He has not raised his voice at me in eleven years. He has looked at me in a certain way twice and I remember both."

npcs.bio: Stands behind the chair. Has never sat in it and would like that noted.

npcs.name: Teddy

lines.text: I picked this suit. Out of a book. On my own.
Everybody asks. Nobody believes me. I picked it.

npcs.bio: Pink, like all of them. Says he chose it.

npcs.name: Roy

lines.text: He is in. Door opens on its own. Do not stand in it looking at it, everybody does that.

npcs.bio: Pink, like all of them. Has never said one word about it either way.

npcs.name: Deuce

lines.text: Three is not a floor you get out on by accident.
I pressed the button.
Yeah. That is the accident I meant. Go on then, he is at the far end.

npcs.bio: On the lift. Has been told which floor you are allowed on and has not been told why.

npcs.name: Junior

lines.text: Nine of us in here Tuesdays. He takes the front and he uses the board.
What is on the board?
Names, mostly. It gets wiped.

npcs.bio: In the training room, which on this floor is a room where people actually train.

npcs.name: The One In The Cream Suit
npcs.bio: One of Tonya Soprani’s. Walks out to the desert on a Thursday and has never once looked behind him, which is not the same as never looking.

npcs.name: The One Carrying It
npcs.bio: The other one. Carries whatever is being carried and is therefore always four steps behind.

npcs.name: Dinah Rose

lines.text: Thank you. You are very kind.
That was beautiful.
It was the same as last night and it will be the same tomorrow. That is the job, and I am not complaining about it.
Sonny goes on after me. Sonny always goes on after me. Ask him how long that has been true and watch his face do something.

npcs.bio: Sings the early set at the big WIN, in a red dress, under a screen that spends the whole number telling the room how much the casino loves it.

npcs.name: Wanda
npcs.greeting: Tickets, popcorn, something cold. In that order, usually.
npcs.bio: Sells the tickets and the popcorn, which in a room this size is one job. Has watched the same act eleven hundred times and can tell you which night it went wrong.

npcs.name: Mel Kranz
npcs.greeting: Licence, ring, flowers, cake. And I will witness it, which is the only one of those that is free.
npcs.bio: Licences, rings, flowers and cake, and he is the witness as well, which in a building this size is one job. Has signed the bottom of four thousand of them and can still spell every name back to you.

A bouquet, out of the cooler

npcs.name: Sunny

lines.text: THERE you are.
You are late for your shift and we are super busy, get to grilling!

topics.label: Remind me how to cook breakfast again???
replies: ...You are joking.
Ticket comes up, you read it, you pour what it says onto the flat-top. Pancakes go on first because they take the longest.
Then you WATCH it. When it bubbles all over and the edge goes dull, that is the moment. Flip it then, not before it and not after it.
And you send the plate while it is hot. A cold plate is a plate that comes back.
That is the whole of it and I have watched grown men cry over it. Go on.

topics.label: I don't work here, sorry.
replies: Everybody who has ever stood there has said that.
Apron is on the hook when you change your mind. We are open all day. That is the entire idea.

npcs.bio: Runs the grill at the Breakfast All Day. Nobody has called him anything but Sunny since about nineteen sixty and he has stopped correcting them.

npcs.name: Plum

lines.text: Busy today?
Every day, near enough. The library reshelves on a Thirdday and the whole avenue queues for it.

npcs.bio: Walks the north avenue most days. Has opinions about the state of the paving.

npcs.name: Mauve

lines.text: Anything I should know?
Mind the crossing. Everyone cuts the corner at the crest and nobody looks.

npcs.bio: Crosses the square four times a day and could not tell you why.

npcs.name: Iris

lines.text: Good morning.
It is, actually. The lilac took at last — third year of trying.

npcs.bio: Grew the lilac in half the window boxes on this street.

npcs.name: Brother Cinnabar

lines.text: Are you of the church?
Of the order, yes. We are not only for the nave. Somebody has to see the town.

npcs.bio: Acolyte of the Church of Gaya. Past the novitiate. Trusted with a shrine of their own.

npcs.name: Amethyst

lines.text: Waiting for something?
A crate. Due on the last ship, and the last ship has been and gone.

npcs.bio: Waiting on a delivery that was due on the last ship.

npcs.name: Lilac

lines.text: You know everyone here.
By their walk, mostly. Faces change. Nobody changes how they cross a square.

npcs.bio: Knows every fox on the square by their walk before their face.

npcs.name: Sister Damson

lines.text: You are a long way from the church.
Sent out to look at it. Hard to pray for a town you have only seen from a window.

npcs.bio: Novice of the Church of Gaya. Newly of the order. Still gets the early bells.

npcs.name: Orchid

lines.text: Keeping well?
Between jobs. Have been for a year. It suits me better than the jobs did.

npcs.bio: Between jobs, cheerfully, for about a year now.

npcs.name: Marty Kessel

lines.text: What is on the card?
Two drink minimum, ten o clock, room at the back.
I have handed out about forty thousand of these and I could not tell you the name of the act. It is on the card. I have just never read it.

npcs.bio: Hands out cards for a lounge act at the far end of the street. Has never been to it.

npcs.name: Bernice Oyelaran

lines.text: Long walk.
Fremont to the desert and back. Doctor said walking.
I have done it so many times I know which bulbs are out. Nobody ever changes them and nobody ever needs to. They have been out the same length of time as everything else here.

npcs.bio: Walks the length of the boulevard every night, top to bottom and back. Says it is for her knees.

npcs.name: Curtis Rand

lines.text: Busy night?
Four so far. Same song four times.
They all cry at the same line and I have stopped hearing it. Ask me what the line is. I could not tell you and I have sung it nine thousand times.

npcs.bio: Sings at the chapel for whoever is getting married. Walks between the two ends of the street in the suit.

npcs.name: Ana-Lucia Prieto

lines.text: Finished for the night?
Finished. Back at eight.
It is always about to be eight. I have stopped looking at the clock over the door because the clock over the door is not helping.

npcs.bio: Off shift from a table somewhere and walking home the long way, which is the only way there is.

npcs.name: Duke Sorrentino

lines.text: Any good?
Best in town. I would not say it if it was not.
Have I eaten there? ...I carry the board. That is a different question and I notice you asked the second one.

npcs.bio: Carries a board advertising an all-you-can-eat that nobody has ever come back from disappointed.

npcs.name: Hazel Minter

lines.text: Trying to get somewhere?
The airport. There is never a cab on this stretch.
Which is strange, because there is never anyone in the cabs either. I have watched about nine go past. All empty. None of them stopping.

npcs.bio: Waiting for a cab. Has been up and down this side of the street looking for one for a while now.

npcs.name: Teddy Zhang

lines.text: Selling film?
Two rolls a dollar. Everybody buys, nobody develops.
I have never once had a person come back and show me a picture. Not once. And you would, would you not. If it came out.

npcs.bio: Sells film to tourists out of a case. Does the run from the chapel end to the wheel and back all evening.

npcs.name: Lorna Fisk

lines.text: On a break?
Fifteen minutes. I come out here for the sky.
That is the joke, is it not. I come outside to look at a sky that has not changed either. But it is a bigger room, and some nights that is enough.

npcs.bio: On her fifteen minutes, walking it off outside because inside there are no windows and no clocks.
